title: `UPPER` and `LOWER` use full Unicode mappings
verdict: full mappings (`ß` to `SS`, final sigma); sverify raises on non-ASCII
description: `UPPER('straße')` is `STRASSE`, `UPPER('ﬁ')` `FI`, `LOWER('İ')` `i̇` (two code points), `LOWER('ΣΑΣ')` `σας` with a final sigma, `UPPER('ǆ')` `Ǆ`. A collation (`COLLATE 'en-ci'`) changes comparisons, not these functions.
reference: `upper`, `lower` with `char_set: UTF8` and full mappings. Whether Snowflake's tables match Rust's in every case is not documented, so sverify's SQL raises on non-ASCII text (#70). Before this PR that raise was a cast to `VARCHAR`, which never fails, so the SQL returned the message as the value (`eval-cast-raise-varchar`); it now raises (`writer-raise-str`).

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT upper('straße'), lower('İ'), upper('ǆ'), initcap('ǆa'), lower('ΣΑΣ'), upper('ﬁ'), upper('é')
evidence.observed: (STRASSE, i̇, Ǆ, Ǆa, σας, FI, É)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
